coverage_note: Chapter Four (§§ 27-32), where care is introduced and worked out. §§ 19-26, 33-36 carry term hits and have not been extracted; see synthesis/STATUS.md.

units.claim: The being-structure of in-being that the analysis has been driving at is named care, and the explication is ordered into four phenomena with care last.
units.quote: Heidegger names the being-structure sought *care* (Sorge), and orders the explication of in-being fourfold: the phenomenon of *uncoveredness*, *falling* as a basic movedness of Dasein, the structure of *uncanniness* (from being-at-home — familiarity), and *care*.

units.claim: Disposedness is derived from care: the world is experienced as threatening or unthreatening only because Dasein is itself care, and not because a caring Dasein apprehends it so.
units.quote: And only because *Dasein is itself, at itself, care* is the world experienced in its threateningness, its significance.

units.claim: Care is the term for the being of Dasein as such, with the formal structure: a being to which, in its being-in-the-world, this being itself is at issue.
units.quote: Care is the term for the being of Dasein *simpliciter*, with the formal structure: *a being to which, in its being-in-the-world, this being itself is at issue*.

units.claim: Care is marked a pre-structure and explicitly the penultimate phenomenon, with time named as the last nexus of the being of Dasein.
units.quote: Heidegger marks it as a *pre-structure* (Urstruktur) in the sense of Dasein itself — not the *last* nexus of the being of Dasein (that will be time), but the *penultimate* phenomenon through which the proper being-structure can be reached.

units.claim: Concern, which carried the earlier analysis of everyday commerce with the world, is subordinated to care as one of its being-modes.
units.quote: *concern* (Besorgen) is only a being-mode of care — care qua structure of Dasein *is* in-being as concern; caring that is in the world is *eo ipso* concern.

units.claim: The total formal structure of care is given in two moments: being-ahead-of-itself, and always-already-being-alongside something.
units.quote: So the total structure of care in the formal sense: *the being-ahead-of-itself of Dasein in its always-already-being-alongside something*.

units.claim: The not-yet-having belonging to being-out-for is named want or privation and distinguished from a sheer objective not-having.
units.quote: which Heidegger names *want* or *privation* (Darben): not a sheer objective not-having, but always a not-having *of something one is out for*

units.claim: Urge and hang are founded modifications of care in which one moment predominates and covers the rest; care is the condition of their possibility and is not composed out of them.
units.quote: Urge is a being-mode of care — the *not-yet-freed* care — but care is *not* an urge

units.claim: Heidegger dates his first striking on the phenomenon of care to seven years before the course, in work on the ontological foundations of Augustinian anthropology.
units.quote: he first struck on the phenomenon of care seven years earlier while trying to reach the ontological foundations of Augustinian anthropology

units.claim: Care is the primary wholeness of Dasein's being-constitution; the equiprimordial structures belong to it rather than composing it.
units.quote: Care is thus the *primary wholeness* of the being-constitution of Dasein, which as this wholeness lays itself in each case into this or that way of its being-able-to-be

absences.expected_because: The section states the neglect of the question of the being of the intentional as the decisive omission of the phenomenology being criticized — the question § 31 answers with care. No term of the family occurs here.
Conscience and being-guilty are treated as Dasein-phenomena of the same rank as the death analysis of § 34, which does work in the vocabulary of care. This section does not use it at all.
